title: Primitive binding and output hashing strategy
body:
Purpose and summary:

This note proposes a lightweight pattern for: (a) producing stable, collision-resistant module outputs for VPC/IAM/EKS primitives; (b) encoding a deterministic 'binding id' via hashing to make downstream references robust across module refactors and upgrades; and (c) a practical upgrade/migration playbook to roll modules forward without breaking consumers or manual state surgery where possible.

Why we need this
- Current module upgrades often rename outputs or change output shapes; consumers (other modules, ops scripts) rely on outputs by name and occasionally by implicit assumptions.
- In large on-prem/VPC deployments the terraform state touches many teams; manual state edits are high-risk. We need a reproducible way to: stabilize identities for resources (logical binding), and allow module interface evolution.

Design goals
- Deterministic: same inputs => same binding id; stable across minor code reorganizations that don't change inputs.
- Opaque but debuggable: binding id is a hash; human-readable debug fields still emitted.
- Non-breaking defaults: modules should continue to export legacy outputs for a deprecation window.
- Minimal operator work for upgrades; prefer plan/apply flows and scripted state moves over ad-hoc tfstate edits.

Core proposal (high level)
1) Add a computed output 'binding_id' defined as: base64url(sha256(join("|", [module_path, var.namespace, var.name, var.cluster_id, optional var.salt])))
   - module_path: local constant set in module (e.g. "redwood.vpc.primitive") to provide namespace isolation across modules.
   - var.namespace & var.name: user-provided logical names (recommended: environment, logical-app-name)
   - var.cluster_id: optional cluster identifier for multi-cluster segregation
   - optional var.salt: admin-provided stable salt when migration must fix collisions

2) Output naming strategy: canonical outputs exported as: "rdw_<primitive>_<short>" (e.g. rdw_vpc_id, rdw_public_subnet_ids). Keep legacy outputs (vpc_id) for one release cycle and mark deprecated in docs.

3) Output metadata map: add a small string output 'rdw_output_meta' containing a JSON string with keys: {"binding_id":"...","proto_version":"v1","inputs_hash":"..."}. This is useful for operators to programmatically validate compatibility during upgrade.

Example variable and output list (text table)
Variables (recommended minimal set):
- name (string): logical name for primitive; mandatory
- namespace (string): org/env grouping; default "default"
- cluster_id (string): optional; default ""
- tags (map): optional tags passed to resources
- salt (string): optional stable salt for special cases

Outputs (canonical):
- rdw_binding_id (string)  --> computed hash described above
- rdw_binding_namespace (string) --> var.namespace
- rdw_binding_name (string) --> var.name
- rdw_vpc_id (string)  --> main resource id
- rdw_public_subnet_ids (list(string))
- rdw_private_subnet_ids (list(string))
- rdw_output_meta (string) --> small JSON blob (see above)
- legacy outputs (kept): vpc_id, public_subnet_ids (deprecated)

Terraform snippet (usage example):
module "vpc_core" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//vpc?ref=refs/tags/v1.4.0"
  name = var.app_name
  namespace = var.env
  cluster_id = local.cluster_id
}

resource "redwood_provider_binding" "vpc" {
  binding_key = module.vpc_core.rdw_binding_id
  vpc_id = module.vpc_core.rdw_vpc_id
}

Upgrade & migration playbook (practical steps)
- Preflight: run `terraform plan` with the new module in a sandbox workspace; capture outputs and rdw_output_meta for existing state.
- Backfill outputs: if migrating from modules that didn't produce rdw_binding_id, run a small one-time apply of a helper module that computes binding_id from existing inputs and writes a new (non-resource) output into state using `terraform state replace-provider` pattern or `terraform apply` against a helper module that creates local_file with the id. Documented script: scripts/backfill-binding.sh in infra repo.
- Compatibility window: keep legacy outputs for 2 releases (approx 6 weeks) and add deprecation notes in module changelog and console notices.
- State move when required: if module refactor renames the root module address, use `terraform state mv` scripted and gated in CI to map old addresses -> new addresses using mapping derived from rdw_binding_id. Example: `terraform state mv module.old_vpc.aws_vpc.main module.vpc_core.aws_vpc.main` after validating rdw_binding_id in both states.
- Rollback plan: keep previous module version pinned in a rollback branch, keep tfstate snapshots. Automated test harness must validate that the binding_id round-trips and that consumer modules resolve the new rdw_* outputs.

Testing checklist (CI + manual)
- Unit: module unit tests verify binding_id is stable for given inputs (mocked locals).
- Integration (staging): apply module, capture rdw_output_meta and downstream consumer lookups.
- Upgrade test: simulate module upgrade, perform state mv if needed, rerun apply, assert no resource replacements for primary infra resources.
- Chaos: simulate partial failure of apply and confirm rollback path and manual state reconcile steps are documented.

Edge cases and open questions
- Multi-tenant collisions: risk low but possible if salts are absent and users choose identical namespace/name. Mitigation: document best practice to include cluster_id and org prefix.
- Canary consumers: how to coordinate dependent modules that reference legacy outputs? Propose a small compatibility module (`rdw_compat`) that maps legacy outputs to rdw_* names.
- Secret-bearing inputs: do not include secrets in binding_id inputs; only use immutable logical identifiers.
- Proto_version bumping: when we change the binding algorithm (v1 -> v2), how to migrate? Proposal: expose both rdw_binding_v1 and rdw_binding_v2 for a transition window and publish a migration script.

Implementation notes and TODOs
- Add helper library in infra repo providing a terraform-local function shim (via external data source) to compute the sha256+base64url in a consistent way across providers. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789)
- Create `scripts/backfill-binding.sh` and `scripts/state-migration-plan.md` in infra tooling repo.
- Add module CHANGELOG template entries for deprecation of legacy outputs.
- Schedule an eng-ops runbook review with SRE and Solutions Eng.

Appendix: quick command recipes
- compute local binding id (dev): `python -c "import hashlib,base64; s='redwood.vpc.primitive|prod|payments||'; print(base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(s.encode()).digest()).decode().rstrip('=') )"`
- find modules missing rdw_binding_id in state: `terraform state list | xargs -n1 -I{} sh -c 'terraform state show {} | grep rdw_binding_id || echo {}:missing'`

References and related artifacts:
- INF-6421: RFC for output stability
- infra PR #789: helper hashing function and initial module updates

Questions for review meeting:
- agree on default proto_version string format? (v1 vs 2025-01)
- locking window for deprecation of legacy outputs: 2 releases ok?
- operator comfort with scripted state mv; should we automate mapping generation?

Notes to self (working items):
- draft the backfill script and run against staging cluster A (eu-west-1 on-prem lab)
- add sample consumer mapping module `rdw_compat` and test with two downstream repos

-- Sofia
